A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same formal analysis and Dual-Channel GNN framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching renamed concepts and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-classification experiments, channel-removal and aggregation ablations, OOD evaluations, and quantitative and qualitative explanation analyses in Section 7 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds runtime measurements, hyperparameter sensitivity results and DIR/DC-DIR comparisons in Appendices C.1–C.3.

M1.justification: The SE-GNN channel, sparse linear rule channel, annealed LEN aggregation and training procedures are retained. v1 already describes SMGNN's GSAT extractor and GISST loss in Appendix B.2. DC-DIR applies the existing framework to another backbone without a newly documented algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three synthetic tasks, five real-world datasets and AIDSC1 variant, including the same size and topology OOD scenarios in Appendix B.1. The added experiments reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated DIR baseline and its DC-DIR augmentation across the five existing real-world datasets in Table 7. DIR's source was cited in v1, but this comparison was absent. Earlier benchmark and aggregation-ablation comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce runtime measurements in seconds and GOODMotif sweeps over LEN hidden size, depth, sigmoid temperature and GSAT's r. The DIR experiment explicitly uses no hyperparameter tuning. Existing splits, training budgets, predictive metrics and faithfulness evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.1–C.2 add a runtime-overhead analysis on Graph-SST2 and BBBP and a four-factor hyperparameter sensitivity study on GOODMotif. Earlier channel-removal, aggregation, strong-sparsification, faithfulness, OOD and qualitative explanation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten random splits in Appendix B.4 and report variation using ± values. Added tables continue that reporting convention; no increased run count, new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 5–7 add runtime, sensitivity and DIR/DC-DIR results. For example, GOODMotif DC-GSAT accuracy is 90±2 at r=0.5 and 93±1 at r=0.7 or 0.9; DIR/DC-DIR BBBP AUCs are 64±2 and 65±2. All earlier table values and plotted findings are retained after matching renumbered material.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 is restricted from arbitrary existential FOL to positive existential formulas, with the preservation argument revised in Appendix A.2. Proposition 5.4 changes from an if-and-only-if characterization to a necessary condition and removes the restriction to PI explanations contained in R. These materially revise two central formal guarantees, beyond the TE-to-ME renaming.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the abstract and contribution statements to some popular SE-GNNs and explicitly identifies sparsity- and information-bottleneck-based models in the conclusion. This brings the headline characterization into line with limitations already acknowledged in v1. The principal explanation-comparison and DC-GNN contributions remain.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the timing results as limited overhead and the hyperparameter results as robustness, with an exception at r=0.5. Appendix C.3 distinguishes DC-GNN applicability to DIR from guarantees about Minimal Explanations and qualifies its results as untuned. Existing mechanism explanations and principal limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an explicit public GitHub repository link in Section 7, replacing v1's reference to supplementary code. It also documents tested hyperparameter ranges, runtime values and the absence of DIR tuning. Existing implementation, software, hardware and training details are retained; the timing procedure itself remains briefly specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kuperberg (2023) to support the positive-FOL discussion and Spinelli et al. (2023) among related SE-GNN approaches. The Azzolin faithfulness reference is updated to its renamed published version rather than introducing a distinct work. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Trivial Explanations become Minimal Explanations throughout, accompanied by localized rewrites of the abstract, theoretical transitions and conclusion, a clearer SMGNN explanation, and new impact and acknowledgment sections. The main section sequence and most existing appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, extensively resizing and repositioning existing displays. Figure 1 moves earlier and receives an expanded explanatory caption; Table 1 is expanded, and three new experimental tables are added. The sixteen existing figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: The decisive improvement is the correction of central theoretical overclaims: v2 adds the positivity restriction needed by Theorem 4.2's preservation argument and aligns Proposition 5.4 with the necessity direction actually established in Appendix A.6. These changes substantially strengthen the reliability of a paper centered on formal guarantees. Added sensitivity and DIR evaluations and explicit code-access information provide further support, although the runtime protocol remains underspecified.
